Virtual assistant makes me sound like a microwave with a voice chip, but fair enough—if you want choices, we can do choices.

First way is classic fried rice. Heat up whatever oil or butter you have, toss in the cold rice, scramble the eggs right into the middle of the pan, and throw that tired spinach in at the very end so it wilts without turning to absolute mush. A splash of soy sauce or sesame oil pulls it together.

Second is the lazy bowl. Heat the rice in a bowl. Flash-fry the spinach in a skillet for thirty seconds with some salt or garlic, set it on the rice, and then fry the eggs sunny-side up so the yolks break and make a sauce over everything.

Third route is porridge style, kind of like a quick congee. Simmer the rice in a little water or broth until it gets thick and soft, beat the eggs in a cup, and drizzle them in while stirring so you get silky ribbons. Stir in the spinach until it melts into the soup.

Fourth is an egg-and-rice skillet cake. Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt, roughly chop the spinach, and stir the rice right into the raw egg mixture. Pour the whole thing into a hot, oiled pan and cook it low and slow like a frittata until the bottom is golden, then flip it. 

Fifth option: crispy rice pancakes. Same idea as the skillet cake, but you shape them into smaller, flat patties and fry them in a little more oil until the outside is deeply crunchy and the inside stays soft.
